skill.name: Dialogue that moves the story on
skill.why: Every line of talk should push the story forward, not just fill space.
skill.how: Cut the hellos. Keep lines that reveal something, cause trouble or make a choice.

steps.say: The crew is in the galley, waiting for dinner. Here's my first try at their talk.
steps.ask: What has changed after these four lines?

options.reason: Read it again. Does Zed say he found anything?
Nobody mentions trouble. They just chat.

steps.win: Right. Nothing changed. Talk like this just fills space. Real people say it, but stories cut it.

steps.say: Talk in a story is called dialogue. Good dialogue changes something. Now Zed says one line.

show.text: 'I've seen Maxx's van at the jetty,' said Zed.

steps.ask: What does the crew know now?

options.reason: That was the old talk. What place does Zed name?
Zed doesn't mention games. What did he see?

steps.win: Yes! That's news. Now the crew can go to the jetty. The story moves on.

steps.say: News is one way to move a story on. Here are two more ways: trouble and a choice.

show.nudge: That's news. But does anyone have to pick between two things?

show.text: 'Don't tell Wren, but I let the Creature out.'
show.nudge: That starts trouble! But does anyone have to pick between two things?

show.text: 'We can save the egg or the boat. Not both.'

steps.ask: Tap the line that makes someone choose.
steps.win: Yes! Egg or boat? Someone has to pick. News, trouble and choices all move a story on.

steps.say: Careful. Mo's line is loud and excited. Zed says that means it moves the story on.

show.text: 'WOW! This is SO cool!' shouted Mo.

steps.ask: Does Mo's line move the story on?

options.reason: Loud isn't the same as new. What does the crew know or do now?

options.text: Yes. It has an exclamation mark.
options.reason: Marks don't move a story. Ask: what does this line change?

steps.win: Right. Shouting doesn't change anything. Ask: after this line, what is different?

steps.say: With lots of talk, readers can forget who is speaking. So name the speaker.

show.nudge: Those are the words. Who said them?
That's how it was said. Which word tells you who?

steps.ask: Tap the word that tells you who is talking.
steps.win: Yes! Name the speaker when it isn't clear. And start a new line each time a new person talks.

steps.say: Back to the galley. Mo's line just fills space. Let's swap it for one that starts trouble.
steps.ask: Which line should Mo say instead?

options.reason: Another hello. Nothing new happens. What could go wrong?

options.text: 'Yes, a very nice night,' said Mo.
options.reason: Still chit-chat about the night. What would change after it?

options.text: 'Don't panic, but dinner just crawled out of the pot,' said Mo.

steps.win: Yes! Dinner that crawls away is trouble. Now check every line of your own: what does it change?

terms.means: A line that tells the characters something new.
A line that starts a problem, like a secret or a mistake.
A line that makes someone pick between two things.
Hellos and chit-chat. Nothing changes, so cut it.
The name that tells you who is talking.

weDo.frame: The crew is hiding behind a rock, watching Maxx's boat.
weDo.prompt: Which line of talk moves the story on?
weDo.hint: Which line changes what the crew might do next?
weDo.success: An open cage door is news. Now the crew has a chance, and the story speeds up.

options.text: 'Look, he's left the cage door open,' whispered Zed.
'Maxx's boat is really big and shiny,' whispered Tully.
options.reason: The crew can already see the boat. Nothing new is revealed, so nothing changes.

options.text: 'I wish I'd brought a snack,' whispered Gus.
options.reason: It's just chit-chat. Nobody will do anything differently after Gus says it.

weDo.frame: Tully's script for the ship's play has one line that just fills space.
weDo.prompt: Tap the line that fills space. Then choose a line that starts trouble.
weDo.hint: Ask of each line: does anything change after it?
weDo.success: Mo's confession starts trouble, and now Gus's question matters. Every line changes something.

parts.reason: That's news. It changes things, so it stays. Find the line that changes nothing.

parts.tap: 'Then where did the Creature go?' asked Gus.
parts.reason: Gus's question sends the crew searching. It moves the story on.

options.text: 'I left the door open,' said Mo. 'Sorry.'
'Oh no, Wren, that's terrible news,' said Mo.
options.reason: Mo reacts, but nothing new happens. Does anyone have to do anything different after it?

options.text: 'I'm going to miss that Creature so much,' said Mo.
options.reason: It shows Mo cares, but it doesn't start any trouble. What changes after it?

creature.name: Natterflit
creature.blurb: A glider that chatters as it leaps from tree to tree. Each squeak carries it further, so it's never stuck on one branch.

workshop.mentor:
'Don't freak out,' said Mo, 'but the soup is moving.'
Gus leaned over the pot. Something green blinked back. 'That's not soup. That's a Creature.'
'It was soup when I started,' said Mo.
'Then where did the soup go?' asked Gus.
Mo went very quiet. Then he burped, and a tiny bubble of light floated out of his mouth.
'OK,' said Tully. 'Nobody tell Maxx's followers we've got a glowing chef.'
Outside, a drone buzzed past the porthole, its red light blinking.
'Too late,' whispered Zed.
workshop.ask:
Write six to eight lines of talk. Every line changes something.
Stuck? Start with: 'Don't freak out, but...'
Challenge: no 'said'. Show who's talking by what they do.
checklist: Every line brings news, trouble or a choice.
Each new speaker starts a new line.
I named the speaker wherever it wasn't obvious.
I cut every hello and weather chat.
